# Conductor

> Compile-then-execute DAG engine for building visual workflow systems.

Conductor is a Python library for graph-based workflow execution. A node is a class whose typed `run` signature is its interface; a graph is a list of placed nodes whose inputs are bound to other nodes' outputs or to typed-in values; compile turns a graph into an immutable `CompiledGraph` that says everything about it, including what is wrong; the engine runs it as a stream of events, once per row wherever a series arrives. Conductor ships every mechanism and no vocabulary: which value types and which nodes exist is the host's decision.

## Quick Start

Two nodes: one written for a single value, one for a whole series. That difference is the whole of how iteration works here.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from conductor import CompiledGraph, DType, Edges, Graph, GraphNode, NodeDefinition, NodeRegistry, Ref, Result, Series, Static
from conductor.execution.engine import execute_sync
from conductor.widgets import ConnectionList, Textarea


class Text(DType, str):
    id = "text"
    title = "Text"


class Upper(NodeDefinition):
    id = "upper"
    title = "Upper case"
    description = "Upper-cases one text"
    category = "text"

    def run(self, text: Annotated[Text, Textarea(title="Text")]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Result")]:
        return Text(text.upper())


class Join(NodeDefinition):
    id = "join"
    title = "Join"
    description = "Joins every text of a series"
    category = "text"

    def run(self, texts: Annotated[Series[Text], ConnectionList(title="Texts")]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Result")]:
        return Text("+".join(texts))


registry = NodeRegistry()
registry.register(Upper)
registry.register(Join)

graph = Graph(nodes=[
    GraphNode(id="upper", type="upper", version=1, bindings={"text": Static(value=["a", "b", "c"])}),
    GraphNode(id="join", type="join", version=1, bindings={"texts": Edges(refs=(Ref("upper", "result"),))}),
])
compiled = CompiledGraph.from_graph(graph, registry)
assert compiled.is_runnable, compiled.problems

results = execute_sync(compiled)
list(results["upper"]["result"])   # ["A", "B", "C"] — three values typed into one input: it ran once per value
results["join"]["result"]          # "A+B+C" — Series[Text] received the whole series, once
```

## Core Concepts

### The Node Contract

A node is a `NodeDefinition` subclass with `id`, `title`, `description` and `category` (optional `tags`, `docs`), and a `run` method. The typed signature of `run` is the interface; nothing is declared twice.

- **Inputs.** Every parameter an edge can reach is `Annotated[DType, Widget(...)]`. `title`, `description` and `show_handle` are written on the widget and lifted onto the `Input` record. A default makes the input optional. `show_handle=False` closes the input to edges, and it may then declare any pydantic-validatable type.
- **Outputs.** The return annotation declares them. `Annotated[Text, Result(title=...)]` is one output named `result`. A frozen dataclass whose fields are `Annotated[DType, Result(...)]` is one output per field, named by the fields. `Mapping[str, Any]` means the placed node's computed interface names the outputs, returned by name.
- **`Any`** is for a value a node routes without reading. An `Any` output needs a `compute_outputs` override, which types it from what arrives.
- **Open interfaces.** `def run(self, **inputs: Single)` makes every name connected into the node an input, each received as one value; `**inputs: Series` receives each as a whole series.
- **Values, not markers.** A node returns `SKIPPED` on a branch it did not take, and `Asks` when a person must answer. Nothing on the class declares that it skips or asks, except that a `run` which may ask says so in its return annotation: `-> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Decision")] | Asks`.
- **Stateless by contract.** Every call is made on a fresh instance. What a run supplies (a clock, a client, the caller's identity) arrives through `FromRun` parameters, never through the instance.
- The class is checked when it is defined: a missing identity attribute, a parameter without a widget, or a return without a `Result` raises at the class.

### Versions and Policies

Several versions live in one class. An undecorated `run` is version 1; otherwise every version is a method marked `@version(n)`, the current one is the highest number, and by convention its method is the one named `run`. Each version has its own signature and its own `Policy`.

```python
from conductor import Policy, deprecated, upgrade, version

class Greet(NodeDefinition):
    id = "greet"
    title = "Greet"
    description = "Greets a person"
    category = "text"

    @version(1)
    @deprecated(header="Use version 2")
    def run_v1(self, name: Annotated[Text, Textarea(title="Name")]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Greeting")]: ...

    @version(2, policy=Policy(retries=2, delay=0.5, timeout=10, concurrency=4))
    def run(self, first: Annotated[Text, Textarea(title="First")], last: Annotated[Text, Textarea(title="Last")]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Greeting")]: ...

    @upgrade(1, 2)
    def _split_name(values: dict) -> dict:
        first, _, last = values["name"].partition(" ")
        return {**values, "first": first, "last": last}
```

- `Policy(retries=0, delay=1.0, timeout=None, concurrency=8)` — how the engine runs this version. `concurrency` bounds how many rows run at once.
- `@upgrade(a, b)` rewrites values saved against version `a` into what `b` expects; the class collects them into `cls.upgrades`, and `registry.upgrade_path(node_id, a, b)` returns one.
- `@deprecated(header=..., description=..., alternative=..., migration=...)` (all keyword, all optional) on the class retires the node; on a version method, that version.
- `NodeRegistry.register(cls)` requires versions numbered from 1 with no holes and an `alternative` that exists.
- A version whose body is a graph is a `GraphVersion(graph=(GraphNode, ...), interface=Interface(...))`, placed in `versions` like any other. Compile expands it under the placing node's name (`approve/check`), so its inner nodes run as nodes of the one run.

### Field Hooks

Two optional methods say what one placement of a node has, when that depends on what the author configured:

```python
def compute_inputs(self, declared: tuple[Input, ...], values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Input, ...]: ...
def compute_outputs(self, declared: tuple[Output, ...], values: Mapping[str, Any], arriving: Mapping[str, type[DType]]) -> tuple[Output, ...]: ...
```

`declared` is the pinned version's declaration, `values` the typed-in values, `arriving` the type on each connected input. The defaults return `declared`. Compile asks a fresh instance once per placed node, and `compiled.node(node_id).interface` holds the answer. A hook that cannot answer for the values it was given raises `Refuses(code, message)`, which compile reports as a `Problem` on the node.

### Types

A value on an edge has a `DType`: a real class, usually on a builtin, registered by `id` when it is defined.

```python
class Number(DType, float):
    id = "number"
    title = "Number"
```

- `target.accepts(source)` is the one edge question: may a value of type `source` land on an input declared `target`? The default is `issubclass`; a series is judged by its element.
- A `DType` does not convert, does not pick a widget, and formats itself only through `as_text`. `refuses_whole` lets a type refuse to be received whole, with a message naming the fix.
- `describe()` is `{"id", "accepted_as"}`; `registered_dtypes()` lists every type declared so far; `dtype_of(annotation)` reads the type off an annotation.
- `Series[X]` is the one collection: many values of one type on an `Index`. `Series[Series[X]]` does not exist.
- `Index(id, parent=None)` names where a series' rows come from and is compared by `id`. A row is a path: `(i,)` on a root index, `(i, j)` for the j-th row under parent row `(i,)`, so `Index.depth` is the length of its rows.
- `Ref("node.field")` (or `Ref("node", "field")`) is the address of one field on one node.
- `DTypeRef` is the annotation a record uses to hold a declared type and dump it as its `describe()`.

### Bindings

A graph is `Graph(nodes=[...])`, and a placed node is `GraphNode(id=, type=, version=, bindings=, locked=, title=, description=, fields=, display=)`. There is no edge record: each input holds at most one binding.

- `Edges(refs=(Ref("a", "result"), ...))` — the value arrives over edges. Several refs into a `Series[X]` input on different indexes gather into one series; several on one index are a union, and a row two of them cover fails the node with `row_covered_twice`.
- `Static(value=...)` — the author typed the value. A list typed into a scalar input makes the node run once per value.
- No binding — the declared default applies.
- `locked` names inputs no caller of the graph may fill.

`dependencies_of(nodes)` and `is_input_node(node)` are read off the bindings. A node id may not contain `.`, since a `Ref` reads `node.field`.

### Compilation

`CompiledGraph.from_graph(graph, registry)` is the one way to compile. It is pure and never raises for a fault in the graph: everything wrong is a `Problem` (`code`, `message`, `fatal`, `node_id`, `field`, `details`) on the result. Every definition the graph names must be in the registry; a host that loads definitions at run time passes `registry.extended_with({id: cls, ...})`.

Ask it at three scales:

- **The graph** — `problems`, `is_runnable`, `interface` (what the graph takes and returns: the unlocked inputs of nodes nothing feeds, and every output of the nodes nothing reads from, named by address), `execution_order()`, `decisions()`, `expanded(ref)`.
- **One node** — `compiled.node(node_id)` is a `CompiledNode`: `interface`, `iterates_on` (the `Index` it runs once per row of, or `None`), `statics`, `runner`, `dependencies`, `version`, `graph_node`, `embedded_in`, `problems`.
- **One field** — `compiled.field(ref)` is a `CompiledField`: `type`, `index`, `binding`, `condition` (a formula over the decisions upstream: `Condition`, `Atom`, `ALWAYS`), `problems`.

Compile types every unconstrained field from what arrives, asks `accepts` on every edge, decides which nodes run per row, and asks the field hooks. A problem inside an embedded graph is reported on the node the author placed.

### Rows

The engine's unit of work is a node on a row. A node that runs once is one unit; a node iterating on an index is one unit per row, and the engine starts every unit as soon as what it reads exists, so row 1 can finish a whole chain while row 10 is still being produced.

- **Iteration.** A series arriving on a scalar input runs the node once per row. Its outputs are series on the same index.
- **Birth.** A node returning a list on a `Series[X]` output births rows: `(j,)` from a node that runs once, `(i, j)` from its unit on row `(i,)`, on a child index of its own.
- **Reduction.** A `Series[X]` input on a root index receives the whole series once it is complete; on a child index, the rows under each parent row, once per parent row. Inside an embedded graph fed a series, a reduction over that series runs once per outer row.
- **Gather.** Refs on different indexes into a `Series[X]` input collect into a fresh series; skipped sources drop out.
- **A skip has a depth.** `SKIPPED` written at a row skips that row, and the series downstream is sparse; `SKIPPED` above a node's rows skips everything under it. A node whose every row was skipped produced an empty series; a node skipped above its rows did not run and is absent from the results.
- **Concurrency.** A node's rows run at most `Policy.concurrency` at a time, each in a worker thread through `asyncio.to_thread`. The engine sets no limit across nodes, but those threads come from the event loop's default executor, which is bounded (`min(32, cpu + 4)` on CPython) and shared by every node.
- **Time.** A write asks readiness only of the units it concerns, so a run's time grows with its rows.

### Legs and Asking

One call of `execute` is one **leg**. It runs until nothing is runnable and nothing is in flight.

A node that needs a person returns `Asks(questions=(Input(...), ...), prompt=None)`. Its unit waits, everything that reads it waits, and the rest of the graph runs on. When the leg goes quiet it ends `graph_pending` with every waiting unit — node, row, prompt and questions named by address — plus `results` and `cells`. An iterating asking node asks once per row, in one pending set.

Answering is the next leg, and it is `execute` again:

```python
first = [event async for event in execute(compiled)]
ending = first[-1]                                              # type == "graph_pending"
answers = {"approve": {"result": Text("Approved")}}             # a Series per output for a node on rows
second = [event async for event in execute(compiled, cells=ending["cells"], cache=answers)]
```

`cells` is the ledger's record of everything earlier legs produced, so nothing done is done twice; `cache` pre-seeds nodes with complete outputs, reported as `node_complete` with `cached=True`. A person's answer and a reused result are the same statement to the engine. Nothing is checkpointed and nothing resumes.

Values the run supplies arrive by type: a parameter annotated `Annotated[T, FromRun()]` receives the value keyed `T` in `execute(from_run={T: value})`. `Interface.needs` lists them, and a leg that lacks one refuses to start.

### Retries and Timeouts

Retries live on the version's `Policy` and nowhere else; each unit retries on its own.

- A failure is retried when its error is `retryable` (`NodeExecutionError`, `NodeConnectionError`, `NodeTimeoutError` and a plain exception from `run` are; `NodeValidationError` never is) and attempts remain.
- The delay before attempt `n` is `delay * 2 ** (n - 1)`; each retry emits `node_retry` with `row`, `attempt`, `retries`, `error` and `delay`.
- `Policy.timeout` bounds one attempt; expiry is `NodeTimeoutError`.
- `execute(timeout_seconds=300)` bounds the leg and ends it `graph_timeout`; `execute(cancel=asyncio.Event())` stops it with `graph_cancelled` when set.

### Errors

A run-time failure carries an `ErrorCause(code, message, details, row)` — on the exception and on `node_error` / `graph_error`. `row` is the row a node running per row failed on. The codes the engine itself emits are `conductor.errors.CODES`; a node may raise a `NodeError` with a cause of its own.

```
ConductorError
├── CompilationError        execute was asked to run a graph compile found not runnable; carries problems
├── NodeError               one node failed; node_id, original, cause, retryable
│   ├── NodeValidationError     the inputs were wrong (never retried)
│   ├── NodeExecutionError      run raised
│   ├── NodeTimeoutError        the policy's timeout expired
│   └── NodeConnectionError     an external call failed (retried)
├── GraphExecutionError     execute_sync: the graph failed, was cancelled or timed out
└── GraphPendingError       execute_sync: the leg ended pending; carries pending and cells
```

A failed unit fails the run: no further unit starts, and the leg ends at once. A `run` already in its worker thread is not interrupted; it finishes, and what it returns is dropped. Every ending carries `results` and `cells`, so a host can start a new run from a failed one.

### Events

`execute` yields `TypedDict` events (`conductor.execution.events`):

| Event | Carries |
|---|---|
| `node_start` | `node_id` — the node's first unit started |
| `node_progress` | `node_id`, `done`, `total` (`None` until every row exists) |
| `node_complete` | `node_id`, `result` (a `Series` for outputs on rows); `cached: true` only when `cache` supplied the node |
| `node_skipped` | `node_id` — skipped above its rows |
| `node_retry` | `node_id`, `row`, `attempt`, `retries`, `error`, `delay` |
| `node_error` | `node_id`, `error`, `cause` |
| `graph_complete` | `results`, `cells` |
| `graph_pending` | `pending`, `results`, `cells` |
| `graph_error` | `node_id`, `error`, `cause`, `results`, `cells` |
| `graph_cancelled` | `results`, `cells` |
| `graph_timeout` | `results`, `cells`, `elapsed_seconds`, `timeout_seconds` |

A frame carries records (a `Series`, an `ErrorCause`, an `Input`), not their JSON; the host serialises them at its edge. `results` is `{node_id: {output_name: value}}`.

### Saving a Graph

Every record a host saves or sends is a `ConductorModel`, a frozen pydantic model: `Graph`, `GraphNode`, `FieldContent`, `Edges`, `Static`, `Problem`, `ErrorCause`, `Policy`, `Deprecation`, `NodeDescription`, `VersionDescription`, `Input`, `Output`, every widget, `Choice`, `OperatorChoice`, `Index`.

```python
graph.to_path("approval.yaml")          # .json, .yaml or .yml by suffix; anything else is refused
graph = Graph.from_path("approval.yaml")
text = graph.to_yaml(); Graph.from_yaml(text)
graph.model_dump_json(); Graph.model_validate_json(text)
```

A ref stores as its address, `"node.field"`. YAML needs PyYAML (`pip install "syv-conductor[yaml]"`). What compile and the engine build per call — `CompiledGraph`, its views, `NodeVersion`, `GraphVersion`, `Interface` — stays a frozen dataclass. A pydantic model returned from `run` is one value, not one output per field.

### The Palette

`NodeDefinition.describe()` is the one serialisation of a node: a `NodeDescription` with `id`, `title`, `description`, `category`, `tags`, `docs`, `deprecation`, `current` and `versions` (each a `VersionDescription` with `inputs`, `outputs`, `policy`, `open`, `deprecation`). A palette is `[cls.describe() for cls in registry.definitions()]`, dumped through pydantic.

## API Reference

### conductor (top-level)

The node-authoring surface, re-exported from the modules that define it:

- Nodes: `NodeDefinition`, `NodeVersion`, `GraphVersion`, `Policy`, `Deprecation`, `NodeDescription`, `version`, `upgrade`, `deprecated`, `Interface`, `FromRun`, `Input`, `Output`, `Result`, `AnyWidget`
- Values a run returns: `SKIPPED`, `Asks`, `is_skipped`, `is_asking`
- Types: `DType`, `DTypeRef`, `Single`, `dtype_of`, `registered_dtypes`, `Series`, `Index`, `Ref`
- Registry: `NodeRegistry` (`register`, `get`, `contains`, `definitions`, `upgrade_path`, `extended_with`, `runner_for`)
- Graph: `Graph`, `GraphNode`, `FieldContent`, `Binding`, `Edges`, `Static`, `dependencies_of`, `is_input_node`, `CompiledGraph`, `CompiledNode`, `CompiledField`, `Problem`, `Condition`, `Atom`, `ALWAYS`

Everything else is imported from the module that defines it.

### conductor.execution.engine

- `execute(compiled, *, timeout_seconds=300, from_run=None, cache=None, cells=None, cancel=None)` — one leg, as an async generator of events.
- `collect(events)` — drain a stream; return the results, or raise `GraphPendingError` / `GraphExecutionError` for the ending that stopped it.
- `execute_sync(compiled, **kwargs)` — `collect(execute(...))` under `asyncio.run`, for scripts and tests.

### conductor.errors

`ErrorCause`, `CODES`, `ConductorError`, `CompilationError`, `NodeError`, `NodeValidationError`, `NodeExecutionError`, `NodeTimeoutError`, `NodeConnectionError`, `GraphExecutionError`, `GraphPendingError`.

### conductor.model

`ConductorModel` — `to_yaml()`, `from_yaml(text)`, `to_path(path)`, `from_path(path)`, beside pydantic's `model_dump_json` / `model_validate_json`.

### conductor.graph.problem

`Problem`, `problem(code, node_id, field=None, **details)`, `CATALOGUE` (every code compile emits, with its message template and whether it is fatal), `CODES`.

### conductor.widgets

Every control is a frozen model with a `kind`; `AnyWidget` is their union. `title`, `description` and `show_handle` belong to the field and are lifted onto the `Input`.

| Widget | For | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `Text` | one line | `min_length`, `max_length`, `pattern` |
| `Textarea` | several lines | `rows`, `min_length`, `max_length` |
| `TemplateTextarea` | text with placeholders | `rows` |
| `CodeEditor` | source code | `language`, `min_length`, `max_length` |
| `Dropdown` | one of a vocabulary | `choices` (`Choice(id, title, element)`) |
| `EntityDropdown` | choices the host resolves | `entity_kind`, `multiple` |
| `Number` | a number typed in | `min_val`, `max_val`, `step`, `integer_only` |
| `Range` | a number on a slider | `min_val`, `max_val`, `step` |
| `Switch` | a boolean | — |
| `DatePicker` | a date | `min_date`, `max_date`, `seed` |
| `FileUpload` | uploaded files | `accept`, `max_size_mb`, `multiple` |
| `List` | values typed by hand | `min_items`, `max_items` |
| `Tags` | free-form labels | — |
| `TableInput` | a table typed or pasted in | `min_rows`, `min_columns`, `column_types` |
| `SchemaBuilder` | a schema built field by field | `schema`, `allow_additional`, `field_types` |
| `IfElseBuilder` | conditions from the host's operators | `operators` (`OperatorChoice(id, title, category, arity)`) |
| `ConnectionList` | connected only: a `Series[X]` or `Any` input | — |

Conductor ships no default widget for any type; every input declares its own. The vocabulary inside a control is the host's, as data.

### conductor.registry.discovery

`discover_nodes(package_name, registry)` imports every module in a package so the registrations in it run, and returns how many definitions were added.

### conductor.interface

`Interface` (`inputs`, `outputs`, `returns`, `needs`, `open`; `Interface.of(run)`), `FromRun`, `model_of(inputs)` — the pydantic model a call is validated through.

## Workspace Packages

Three distributions, released in lockstep: `syv-conductor` (import `conductor`), `syv-conductor-nodes` (`conductor_nodes`), `syv-conductor-providers` (`conductor_providers`). `syv-conductor[all]` installs all three.

### conductor-nodes

A standard node library with a four-type vocabulary of its own, `conductor_nodes.types`: `Text`, `Number`, `Flag`, `Json`, and `StdlibNode`, the base that pins `category`.

```python
from conductor_nodes import get_default_registry, register_all

registry = get_default_registry()                         # every node
register_all(registry, categories=["text", "math"])       # or a subset on a registry of your own
```

| Module | Node ids |
|---|---|
| `text` | `text-uppercase`, `text-lowercase`, `text-trim`, `text-length`, `text-concat`, `text-replace`, `text-contains`, `text-split`, `text-join`, `text-reverse` |
| `math` | `math-add`, `math-subtract`, `math-multiply`, `math-divide`, `math-modulo`, `math-round`, `math-min`, `math-max`, `math-abs` |
| `logic` | `logic-if-empty`, `logic-if-equals`, `logic-not` |
| `json_ops` | `json-parse`, `json-stringify`, `json-get` |
| `regex_ops` | `regex-match`, `regex-replace`, `regex-extract` |
| `decision` | `decision` — routes any value to one of two branches on a connected `Flag` |

### conductor-providers

- `conductor_providers.react` — `graph_to_react(graph)` (ReactFlow JSON: the node record under each node's `data`, edges derived from the bindings, positions laid out where none is stored), `react_to_graph(wire)`, `palette_from_registry(registry)`.
- `conductor_providers.fastapi` — `conductor_router(registry, *, prefix, tags, dependencies, from_run, entity_resolver)`: `GET /nodes`, `POST /compile` (every problem), `POST /execute`, `POST /execute-stream` (server-sent events) and `GET /entities/{kind}`. `from_run(request)` returns the values `execute(from_run=...)` supplies; `sse_frame(event)` serialises one event.

## Project Structure

```
packages/
├── conductor/src/conductor/
│   ├── node.py, interface.py, metadata.py, returns.py, model.py
│   ├── dtype.py, dtype_ref.py, series.py, ref.py, widgets.py, errors.py, _sentinel.py
│   ├── registry/        — NodeRegistry, discovery
│   ├── graph/           — model, binding, compiler, compiled, iteration, expand, conditions, problem, topology, views
│   ├── execution/       — engine, ledger, events
│   └── about/           — this reference (python -m conductor.about)
├── conductor-nodes/src/conductor_nodes/
│   └── types, text, math, logic, json_ops, regex_ops, decision
└── conductor-providers/src/conductor_providers/
    ├── react/           — graph, schema, layout
    └── fastapi/         — router, models, sse
```

## Feature Map (finding the right thing)

| You want... | Use |
|---|---|
| A node to read another node's output | `Edges` on the input |
| A value the author types | `Static` on the input |
| A node to run once per item | Connect a series to a scalar input, or type a list into it |
| One call over all items | Declare the input `Series[X]` |
| Several branches merged back per row | Several refs on one index into one input |
| Items from unrelated sources in one list | Several refs on different indexes into a `Series[X]` input |
| Route around a branch | Return `SKIPPED` on the output not taken; share a `choice` |
| Pause for a person's answer | Return `Asks`; answer with `execute(cells=..., cache=...)` |
| A service or identity inside a node | `Annotated[T, FromRun()]` and `execute(from_run={T: value})` |
| Automatic retry on transient errors | `Policy(retries=..., delay=...)` on the version |
| Limit how many rows run at once | `Policy(concurrency=...)` |
| Inputs that depend on configuration | `compute_inputs` |
| Outputs typed from what arrives | `compute_outputs` |
| A saved graph embedded as a node | A `GraphVersion` in the definition's `versions` |
| Common nodes (text, math, …) | `conductor-nodes` |
| Save or load a graph | `Graph.to_path` / `Graph.from_path` |
| A palette for a frontend | `[cls.describe() for cls in registry.definitions()]` |
| A ReactFlow canvas | `conductor_providers.react` |
| HTTP endpoints | `conductor_providers.fastapi.conductor_router` |

## CLI Reference (this document)

This text is available at runtime from any environment with `conductor` installed:

```bash
python -m conductor.about                 # full text (this file)
python -m conductor.about sections        # list section slugs
python -m conductor.about rows            # print a section by slug (prefix/substring match)
```

Or programmatically:

```python
from conductor.about import get_content, list_sections, get_section
```

The wheel bundles this file as `conductor/about/llms.txt`, so downstream projects that install `syv-conductor` can read the reference without cloning the repository.
